samples.summary: Bounds test's "nothing was pushed onto the undo stack" claim is never asserted
samples.evidence: The `refuses %s, and writes nothing` case comments "Nothing reached the document, and nothing was pushed onto the undo stack on the way to the refusal", but the only assertions are `editor.getPageSetup()).toEqual(DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP)` and `store.getDocument().pageSetup).toBeUndefined()`. Both hold even if `writePageSetup` called `docStore.snapshot()` before `assertUsablePageSetup` threw — the snapshot would leave a phantom, no-op undo entry that a later Ctrl+Z burns. Contrast the sibling test in `editor-read-only.test.ts` (`expect(snapshots).toHaveLength(0)`), which does assert exactly this for `pasteFormat`. Nothing in the diff pins the ordering for the page-setup path (e.g. an `editor.undo()` after the throw, checking a prior edit is reverted).

samples.summary: The ruler margin-drag path was rerouted through the new validating writePageSetup, and nothing tests it
samples.evidence: `ruler.onMarginChange` no longer writes directly; it now builds a setup and calls `writePageSetup`, which calls `assertUsablePageSetup` and can now *throw* from inside a pointer-drag callback, and which also copies through `resolvePageSetup`. `onMarginChange` appears only in `src/view/ruler/index.ts` and `src/view/editor.ts` — no test file references it — so the entire ruler→page-setup write path (the one user-facing path that already existed) has no coverage before or after the refactor. A regression here (a drag that throws mid-gesture, or a margin change that no longer reaches the store) would ship green.
searchedFor: grep onMarginChange across packages/docs (only src hits)

samples.summary: No test asserts that a page-setup write actually repaginates (layout invalidation / render)
samples.evidence: `writePageSetup` does `doc.refresh(); invalidateLayout(); render();` after the store write, but every assertion in the new suite reads back through `editor.getPageSetup()` and `store.getDocument()`. If `invalidateLayout()` were dropped, the model would change while the canvas kept the stale paginated layout — a visible defect — and all of these tests would still pass. I found no observable layout/page-count accessor on `EditorAPI` (`grep getPageCount|pageCount` in view/editor.ts returns nothing), so this may be hard to test, but the gap is real.

samples.summary: EditorAPI.pasteFormat's notifyStyleApplied() side effect is untested
samples.evidence: The new API wrapper calls `notifyStyleApplied()` when the paste applied, so toolbar pickers re-read their summaries even though the caret did not move. `editor-format-painter.test.ts` asserts only the returned boolean and the resulting inline style; it never subscribes to `onCursorMove`/style-applied notification. Removing the `if (applied) notifyStyleApplied();` line would leave every new test green while the toolbar's B/I/U/font state silently went stale after a toolbar paint.

samples.summary: Image-src gate is only exercised with inlineImages: true; the default (placeholder) path's new gate is untested for non-data unsafe sources
samples.evidence: `pictured()` hard-codes `opts = { inlineImages: true }`, and the earlier `it.each` also passes `{ inlineImages: true }`. With `inlineImages` false (the default, and what the CLI uses) a `javascript:alert(1)` or `https://…\n` src does not hit the `isDataUri` early return and depends entirely on the new `isSafeImageSrc` call — that combination has no test. Also untested: the C1 range `-` in `UNEMITTABLE_URL_CHARS` (all payloads use tab/LF/CR/space only), so half of that character class could be deleted without a failure.

samples.summary: The URL-safety cases are duplicated between two describe blocks
samples.evidence: The `it.each` blocks added to `serializeMarkdown — inline mapping` (javascript:/data:text/html/data:image/svg+xml/file: image targets, and javascript:/data:/relative hrefs) are re-asserted almost verbatim in the new `serializeMarkdown — URL safety` describe (`drops a %s link target`, `replaces a %s image source`). Duplicate coverage, no added signal.

samples.summary: Toolbar toggle is tested entirely against a hand-rolled editor stub that reimplements the painter buffer
samples.evidence: `makeEditor()` keeps its own `held` flag and its own listener set; `copyFormat`/`pasteFormat`/`clearCopiedFormat` are `vi.fn()`s with local semantics. The tests therefore verify the toggle against a re-implementation of the contract rather than the real `EditorAPI`. That is a reasonable boundary for a UI-wiring test (and `packages/docs/test/view/editor-format-painter.test.ts` covers the real implementation), but the stub could drift from the engine — e.g. if the real `pasteFormat` stopped returning a boolean — with no frontend test noticing.

samples.summary: The mobile overflow-menu entry for Page setup has no test
samples.evidence: The dialog is mounted once at the toolbar root specifically so the mobile `DropdownMenuItem` ("Page setup" under the new "Document" label) can open it without unmounting with the menu — that is the stated reason for the hoisting. `docs-page-setup-dialog.test.tsx`'s `is reachable from the docs toolbar` only clicks the desktop `getByLabelText('Page setup')` button (matchMedia stubbed to `matches: false`, i.e. desktop). The mobile path, which is the one the hoisting exists for, is never exercised.

finding.summary: "the returned setup is a copy" test passes even if getPageSetup() returns the shared DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP by reference
finding.evidence: The test does `const setup = editor.getPageSetup(); setup.margins.top = 1; setup.paperSize.width = 1; expect(editor.getPageSetup()).toEqual(DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP)`. If `getPageSetup()` did NOT copy (e.g. returned `doc.document.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP`), the mutations would land on `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` itself (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:745, whose `paperSize` is `PAPER_SIZES.LETTER` and whose `margins` is a shared literal), so the expected value would be mutated in lockstep with the actual and the assertion would still hold. The test therefore cannot fail for the exact aliasing bug it claims to guard. A meaningful version must compare against a frozen literal (`{paperSize:{name:'Letter',width:816,height:1056}, ...}`) or assert the returned object is not the same reference across two calls. Note it also mutates a module-level constant, which can leak into sibling tests.

verdict.reason: The finding quotes the test as `setup.margins.top = 1; ... expect(editor.getPageSetup()).toEqual(DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP)`, but that comparison does not exist in the repository. The actual test (packages/docs/test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts:116-142) mutates the returned object and then asserts against hard-coded literals on a freshly read setup — `fresh.orientation === 'portrait'`, `fresh.margins.top === 96`, `fresh.paperSize.width === 816` — plus asserts the module constants are unchanged (`DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP.margins.top === 96`, `PAPER_SIZES.LETTER.width === 816`). Those defaults are confirmed at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:738 and 745-749. If getPageSetup returned the shared constant by reference instead of the deep copy it actually performs (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2973 -> resolvePageSetup at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:751-758), the mutations would land on DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP and the literal assertions at lines 130-132 and 137-140 would all fail. The test therefore does discriminate the aliasing bug and is not vacuous; the alleged mutation leak into sibling tests likewise only occurs in the failing case, which lines 137-140 explicitly catch.
